finding.title: New fact on WEAK-REVIEW: the review of the misses can offer FIXED SIGNAL for a signal drawing, then mark it wrong as safety-critical
finding.place: /drill, the review round ('Practice the N items you missed') after a mixed session ('Start here', 'Continue', /drill); both widths, any motion setting. src/core/drill.ts:175-181: when fewer than three other signals are among the misses, distractors() fills the options from the pool of the misses, which holds other kinds (lines 178-179). The pool is the misses because of focusIds at line 228.
finding.steps: To reproduce it exactly, run p26-fixed-signal.mjs with seed 32 at 1440. From page start, Math.random is replaced by s=(s*1664525+1013904223)>>>0 with s=32. Open Home, press 'Start here', pass each learn card, pick the first option on each question, then press 'Practice the 5 items you missed: 5 questions →'. Pick FIXED SIGNAL on review question 1. As a learner: in a mixed session, miss the term FIXED SIGNAL (or ADVANCE, BLOCK, INTERLOCKING or CONTROLLED SIGNAL) and one signal item, with fewer than three other signals missed, then open the review.
finding.happens: Review question 1, 'What signal is this?', shows the drawing of 422 MEDIUM TO CLEAR. The options are FIXED SIGNAL, CROSSOVER, 422 MEDIUM TO CLEAR and INTERLOCKING. Picking FIXED SIGNAL gives 'Not quite.', the tag 'Your answer' and 'Safety-critical — lock this one in.' The app's own entry for FIXED SIGNAL reads 'A signal or sign in a fixed spot that shows a condition affecting how a movement operates.', which is true of every drawn signal. The ruling's premise, 'No right answer is marked wrong', has not been checked for these options. At 390 with seed 129, the drawing of 412 ADVANCE CLEAR TO LIMITED is offered with FIXED SIGNAL, and the same result follows.
finding.should: A signal question offers signal names only. When the misses hold fewer than three other signals, the distractors come from the other signal items of the library, as in a normal session, and never from definitions or rules.
finding.evidence: Browser output of p26-fixed-signal.mjs: seed 32 at 1440 gave the options ["FIXED SIGNAL","CROSSOVER","422 MEDIUM TO CLEAR","INTERLOCKING"], and picking FIXED SIGNAL gave 'Not quite. | 422 MEDIUM TO CLEAR — … | Safety-critical — lock this one in.' Seed 129 at 390 gave the same result for 412. Seed 4242 (p02.out) offered ADVANCE SIGNAL for 412. The model of the real code (a03-review-options.mts) built 3,996 review rounds with 11,808 signal questions: 171 offered one of FIXED, ADVANCE, BLOCK, INTERLOCKING or CONTROLLED SIGNAL, and 42 offered FIXED SIGNAL.

verdict.evidence:
Reproduced on the built app at dc88b14 (vite preview on port 4560, fresh context, Math.random replaced from page start by s=(s*1664525+1013904223)>>>0, r=s/2^32). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-clear-board/97369320-fcc4-5a82-bc9f-093035f8cbac/scratchpad/final-review/verify-journeys-0/v-review.mjs.

Seed 32 at 1440 (s32-1440.out, shot-seed32-1440.png in the same folder): Home, "Start here", a 10-question session answered with the first option each time, then "Practice the 5 items you missed: 5 questions →". Review question 1, "What signal is this?", shows a red/green/red mast signal. The options are FIXED SIGNAL, CROSSOVER, 422 MEDIUM TO CLEAR, INTERLOCKING. Picking FIXED SIGNAL puts "Your answer" and a cross on it and shows "Not quite." The alert region reads "Not quite. Correct answer: 422 MEDIUM TO CLEAR. Safety-critical — lock this one in. Review your misses at the end." The stored profile then has sig.422 at seen 2, correct 0, ease 2.1, due now, so the miss counted. A second run gave the same output.

Seed 129 at 390 (s129-390.out): review question 1 shows 412 with the options 430 DIVERGING, FIXED SIGNAL, 419A LIMITED TO DIVERGING, 412 ADVANCE CLEAR TO LIMITED. FIXED SIGNAL gets the same verdict and alert, and sig.412 is left at correct 0, due now.

Why FIXED SIGNAL counts as a right answer: the app's own entry (public/data/definitions.json:297) reads "A signal or sign at a fixed location indicating a condition affecting the operation of a movement." All 140 aspects in signals.json are drawn as mast (98) or dwarf (42) signals. So the label is true of every drawing the Drill asks about. The project already sets this bar. src/core/drill.ts:29-33 (U-01) does not ask a drawing that has two right names. REVAMP-APPENDIX.md:661 says signal distractors are other signal titles. REVAMP-APPENDIX.md:856 names a true distractor as the failure that marks a trainee who understands as wrong. No paper mentions the case (grep for "fixed signal" across the papers finds nothing), and lead-rulings.md:180 states "No right answer is marked wrong."

Model of the real buildSession on the frozen data (model.ts):
- With the misses sig.422 and def.fixed-signal, the signal question has exactly two options: 422 MEDIUM TO CLEAR and FIXED SIGNAL.
- With one signal, FIXED SIGNAL and 0 to 4 other definitions missed, 3,306 of 3,800 review signal questions offer FIXED SIGNAL.
- In normal sessions, 0 of 3,584 signal questions offer a non-signal option. The fault is in the review round only.

Scope correction: only FIXED SIGNAL is true of every drawing. ADVANCE, BLOCK, INTERLOCKING and CONTROLLED SIGNAL depend on where a signal stands, which a drawing does not show. For those four the finding adds nothing to WEAK-REVIEW. Whether one of them is right for a given aspect is a question for the SME. The severity stays high: an answer that is true by the app's own entry is marked wrong, with the safety-critical alert, and recorded as a miss on a safety-critical item.
verdict.cause: src/core/drill.ts:228 makes the misses the whole item set of a review round. Lines 237-238 and 248 then build byType and ctx.pool from those misses. In distractors() (src/core/drill.ts:177-179), when fewer than three other items of the same type are present, the rest of the options are filled from that pool, which holds definitions and rules. The review is built at src/stations/Drill.tsx:283 with focusIds. The wrong pick is recorded as a miss at src/stations/Drill.tsx:229 (recordAnswer). A miss always counts (answerCounts, drill.ts:153-156).
verdict.fix:
Small, in one file plus one test. In buildSession (src/core/drill.ts), build byType and ctx.pool from the library that a session of the same route draws from: the drillable items of the domain, or of each live domain, with the U-01 and radio-script filters. The misses stay the items that are asked. That is about 8 lines in src/core/drill.ts. Add one unit test in tests/unit/drill.test.ts: a review over sig.422 and def.fixed-signal gives four signal names.

Tested on a copy (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-clear-board/97369320-fcc4-5a82-bc9f-093035f8cbac/scratchpad/final-review/verify-journeys-0/core-fix/drill.ts, compared by weak.ts and same.ts). Over 5,106 random review questions, real code against the patched copy:
- fewer than 4 options: 215 → 0
- a repeated option: 629 → 0
- a non-signal option on a signal question: 372 → 0
- FIXED SIGNAL offered: 5 → 0

Normal sessions are byte-identical for 1,600 seed and route pairs. The 69 unit tests of drill, severity, signal, sr and store pass on the copy. The same change also clears the one-option and repeated-option cases of WEAK-REVIEW. It touches no frozen file and no rule text.
verdict.ruledAlready: WEAK-REVIEW (specs/briefs/lead-rulings.md:180) covers the mechanism ("an option of another kind") and already goes to the final report. Its sentence "No right answer is marked wrong" does not hold for FIXED SIGNAL. That is the new fact, and it moves WEAK-REVIEW into the high class. Report it as an amendment to WEAK-REVIEW, not as a separate defect. Scope: FIXED SIGNAL only.

finding.title: 'Continue' beside 'N due now' mostly asks about new items, so the items that are due wait
finding.place: Home main control 'Continue' (goes to /drill); the domain tiles behave the same; returning learner, both widths. src/core/drill.ts:239 (due = items.filter(i => isDue(...))) with src/core/sr.ts:30 (isDue(undefined) is true). The comment at drill.ts:250 says new items should fill the session after the due items.
finding.steps: Seed a profile with 70 answered items, 33 of them drillable and due now (returning-profile.json from mkprofile.mts). Open Home: it says 'Continue' and '33 due now'. Press Continue and play the session.
finding.happens: The session shows 8 learn cards and 10 questions: 8 about new items and 2 about due items ('New items started: 8'). Home then says '39 due now'. Over 2,000 sessions on this profile, the real selection asked on average 1.9 due items and 8.1 new items, and 206 sessions (10 %) asked no due item at all. The cause: an item with no stored state counts as due, so every new item lands in the first bucket, 'due & in-band'.
finding.should: Due items come first and new items fill the rest of the session, as the comment in the same function says. The count beside 'Continue' then names the work that 'Continue' does.
finding.evidence: p09.out: 'Home: Continue / 33 due now', 'learn cards 8 questions 10', end 'New items started: 8', 'Home after … 39 due now'. a02-continue.mts: meanDueItems 1.934, meanNewItems 8.066, sessionsWithNoDueItem 206 of 2000; per domain, for example definitions: 10 due, 1.83 due items asked per session. git show 49d3ba0: Home had no 'Continue' and no due count; the selection lines were the same then (Drill.tsx:96, :107).
finding.files: src/core/drill.ts (one line). It changes the selection, so the owner rules first.

verdict.evidence:
Reproduced on the built app and in the code. The tree is unchanged (dc88b14, clean). My files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-clear-board/97369320-fcc4-5a82-bc9f-093035f8cbac/scratchpad/final-review/verify-journeys-1/.

1. Built app (vite preview on 4562, now stopped). I made the profile by simulating real use, not by hand: a fresh start, then 4 "Continue" sessions the day before with 80% right (profile-day1.json, made by sim.mts).
- At 1440 and at 390, Home shows "Continue" and "40 due now".
- Continue opens #/drill. The session has 8 learn cards and 10 questions. A diff of the stored profile shows 10 items asked: 2 were due at the start and 8 were new.
- The tiles do the same. "The words" at 1440 (16 definitions due): 1 due item, 9 new. "Signals" at 390: 3 due, 7 new. Outputs: probe-day1-*.out.

2. The real buildSession over 1000 seeds on that profile asks 2.81 due items and 7.19 new items per session. 33 of the 1000 sessions ask no due item.

3. A 14-day run of a learner who only presses Continue (2 sessions a day, 80% right, 3 seeds; sim2.out):
- Home's morning count climbs 31, 53, 59, ... to 72-87.
- A due item is asked on average 2.7-3.1 days after its due time (p90 6.3-7.4 days).
- With due items first (a patched copy, core-b), the count stays at 7-32 and the average delay is 0.3-0.4 days (p90 about 1 day). The cost: 79-86 new items started instead of 130-135.
- The mix is worst in the first days. From about day 4 a session holds more due items than new ones, as the 139 tier-1 items of the 200-item pool run out.

4. Cause: "due" means two things.
- Home counts only items with a stored state (store.ts:353-362, shown at Home.tsx:35-36).
- The selection counts an item with no state as due (sr.ts:30). So every new item in the tier band shares the first bucket with the due items (drill.ts:239, :252), and the shuffle draws 10 from that mix.
- The selection is unchanged since before the wave (49d3ba0 Drill.tsx:96, :107-113). New items were already in `due` in e16a838. The wave's rows U-26 and U-27 put the count beside the control.

5. Intent: REVAMP-APPENDIX.md:319-320 and :336, the record the tier order came from, says "due-first", "surfaces what you're about to forget" and "still due-first so retention is preserved". UX-10 asks for "Continue" with the count of items due. So this is a defect, not a matter of taste.

Corrections to the finding:
(a) drill.ts:250 does not say that new items fill after the due items. It names not-due items as the filler and is unclear; cite the REVAMP record instead.
(b) The jump right after the session (33 to 39) comes from the probe's wrong picks (2 of 10 right). If the learner answers right, the count drops by the due items answered right, and the new items add to the next day's count. The real harm is the climb over days.
(c) The finder's profile has states that grade() cannot produce (seen 2, correct 1, interval 6). A profile from simulated use shows the same thing.
(d) The one-line fix is not right. It puts new items in the same bucket as items that are not yet due. When few items are due, the rest of the session becomes a random mix of new items and not-due practice, where a right answer counts for nothing. It also starts fewer new items (70-74 in 14 days, against 79-86 for the fix below).

Severity: medium. This is the main control of every returning learner. Its count does not describe the session, and the review schedule slips by days in the first weeks. It is not high: no wrong content, no right answer marked wrong, no lost progress, no blocked learner.
verdict.cause: src/core/drill.ts:239 `const due = items.filter(i => isDue(profile.items[i.id]));` together with src/core/sr.ts:30 (isDue(undefined) is true). Every item the learner never answered lands in the first bucket at drill.ts:252, beside the stored due items. Home's count, src/core/store.ts:353-362 (dueNow), counts only stored states and is shown beside "Continue" at src/stations/Home.tsx:35-36.
verdict.fix:
A small change in one file, src/core/drill.ts. The owner rules first, because it changes the selection. The pacing trade-off (fewer new items while a backlog stands) is also the owner's call, possibly with the SME.

1. Line 239: `const due = items.filter(i => !!profile.items[i.id] && isDue(profile.items[i.id]));`
2. Line 253: split into two buckets, new items before the items that are not yet due:
`...shuffle(items.filter(i => tierOK(i) && !due.includes(i) && !profile.items[i.id]), rng),` then
`...shuffle(items.filter(i => tierOK(i) && !due.includes(i) && !!profile.items[i.id]), rng),`
3. Update the comment at line 250.

Checked on a copy in scratch:
- The 16 drill unit tests pass.
- A fresh profile gets the same session as today, seed for seed (8 routes x 300 seeds), so the first session and the smoke seeds do not change.

Add one unit test that pins a due item being chosen before a new one.
verdict.ruledAlready: None. SESSION-LENGTH covers the length of a first session, not the mix of due and new items for a returning learner. U-44 moved the selection with no change of behaviour, and no approved row puts due items before new ones. So this is an older defect made visible by the U-26/U-27 words. Like RETRY-RESTART and WEAK-REVIEW, it belongs in the final report as a found defect for the owner's ruling.

finding.title: After Reset or Load in Settings, the open Yard still shows the old job marks, and an open session counts the loaded progress as its own gain
finding.place: /yard with the Settings dialog over it, both widths. yardSim.js builds the picker only at mount and after a win (buildPicker, lines 822-850, and the call in recordWin). Same class in the Drill (startMastery in buildSession) and in the Radio test (startRef in RadioTest.tsx).
finding.steps: (a) Open /yard with a profile in which p0-1 and p0-2 are done. Open Settings, press Reset and confirm. (b) As a new learner, open /yard. In Settings press 'Load a file', choose a file with those two wins, confirm and press Done. (c) Answer 2 calls in 'Call it yourself', load a file, then finish the run.
finding.happens: (a) The stored profile is gone, but the picker still says '✓ Make up the cut · par 5 · your best 5 moves' and '✓ Add to the cut · par 5 · your best 7 moves' until the learner leaves the Yard or wins a job. (b) The stored profile holds both wins, but the picker still says '→ Make up the cut · par 5', with no ✓ and no record; the next visit shows them. (c) The end of the Radio run says 'moved your Radio mastery: +4% → 4%' after 4 of 14 right; the 4 % came from the file. The Drill shows the same: 'Signals: +2% → 2%', and 'Items due again … 1 in 3 days', a date from the file.
finding.should: After a reset or a load, the open station shows the progress that is stored now. The Yard rebuilds its picker. A running Drill or Radio session reads its start values again, or starts over.
finding.evidence: p10-yard.out: 'after Reset … stored profile null … picker now: ✓ Make up the cut · par 5 · your best 5 moves | ✓ Add to the cut …'. p18-yard-load.mjs: 'after load, same visit: → Make up the cut · par 5 …', stored yard completed [p0-1, p0-2]; 'next visit: ✓ Make up the cut …'. p24-load-mid.mjs: the Radio and Drill end lines quoted above.
finding.files: src/stations/imperativeStation.ts, src/stations/yardSim.js (picker refresh); Drill.tsx and RadioTest.tsx for the end lines

verdict.evidence:
Reproduced on the built app at dc88b14 (port 4564), with my own probes and my own progress file. Probes and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-clear-board/97369320-fcc4-5a82-bc9f-093035f8cbac/scratchpad/final-review/verify-journeys-2/.

1. Yard, Reset, at 1440 with a mouse and at 390 with touch (v1-yard.mjs, v1-yard.out). The stored profile has p0-1 and p0-2 done. After Reset and confirm, Settings closes and the page stays on #/yard. The stored profile is null. The picker still says "✓ Make up the cut · par 5 · your best 5 moves | ✓ Add to the cut · par 5 · your best 7 moves | → Across the ladder · par 5". The next visit says "→ Make up the cut · par 5 | Add to the cut · par 5 | …".

2. Yard, Load, both widths, new learner. After Load and Done, the stored yard holds completed [p0-1, p0-2] with both records. The picker still says "→ Make up the cut · par 5 | Add to the cut · par 5 | …". The next visit shows the ✓ marks.

3. New fact (v4-yard-win.out): after the Load, a win does not repair the picker. A win of "Make up the cut" at par gives the banner "Job done. ✓ Par! 5 moves — 2 couplings, clean · your best: 5 moves, 2 couplings". The picker on the same screen still says "→ Make up the cut · par 5". recordWin rebuilds the picker only when the record changes. So the finder's "until the learner wins a job" holds after a Reset only.

4. Radio test (v2-radio.out). With no Reset or Load, a new learner's run ends with "+2% → 2%", which is right. In the Load run, a new learner gets 2 calls right, then loads a file with 3 Radio calls at full familiarity. The stored Radio mastery goes from 0.5 to 23.1. All later calls are answered right. The end says "moved your Radio mastery: +24% → 24%". The calls after the load added 1.3 points. In the Reset variant, the profile starts at 23.1 % and Reset comes after call 2. The run is 14 of 14 right, and the end says "moved your Radio mastery: -22% → 2%".

5. Drill /drill/signals (v3-drill.out). The learner answers 2 questions, then loads a file with 10 signal items at full familiarity. The stored Signals mastery goes from 0.1 to 20.4. The end tile says "2 / 10 Signals: +18% → 18%". The answers after the load lowered it by 2 points, to 18.4.

7. Age. The Reset path is older than the wave. At 49d3ba0 the picker is built only at mount and after a new completion, and the Drill and Radio test keep a start value of the same kind. Load (U-18, commit 5c8e10c) is new in Wave 2c and adds a second way into the same state.

8. Fix trial. I built a copy in the scratch folder (fixcopy/, vite build there, tsc clean) with the fix below and served it on port 4565. I ran the same probes (fix-trial.out):
- The picker is right after Reset and after Load, at both widths, and it stays right after the win.
- Drill after a Load: the session starts over, and the end says "5 / 10 Signals: +0% → 21%".
- Radio: the station comes back on the Guided tab. A new run ends "+1% → 24%" after a Load and "+2% → 2%" after a Reset.
- Focus stays on "⚙ Settings". 0 page errors.

Both servers are stopped. The tree has no change.

Severity stays medium. Each case puts a false text on the screen:
- a ✓ and a record that the Reset just cleared;
- "→" on a job that the banner calls done;
- a session gain that came from the file or the Reset.
No progress is lost. The stored profile is right. It needs a Reset or a Load while a station is open, and the Settings button is in the title bar of every route.
verdict.cause:
- src/stations/yardSim.js:852: buildPicker reads ctx.profile. It runs only at mount (:880) and after a win that changes the record (:657).
- src/stations/imperativeStation.ts:54: on each render the bridge writes the new profile into ctx, but it tells the island nothing.
- src/state/AppContext.tsx:267-278 (resetProgress) and :305-315 (replaceProgress): each one replaces the profile with a new object that has a new createdAt.
- src/stations/Drill.tsx:80-85: the session and its startMastery are built once per [content, domain]. :144 takes the gain from that start value.
- src/stations/RadioTest.tsx:92-96: the start value is read once per run. :134-135 takes the gain from it.
verdict.fix:
Small fix, tried on a copy: one file, three lines.
- In src/App.tsx, Shell, read `const { profile } = useApp();`.
- Key the routed view on the profile's createdAt as well as the path: `<RenderGuard key={`${location.pathname} ${profile.createdAt}`}>` (App.tsx:184).

A Reset and a Load each give a new createdAt (freshProfile; LOAD-NEW-PROFILE), so the open station mounts again from the stored progress. Answers, wins and the route recompute keep createdAt, so nothing else mounts again.

The cost: the open station starts over. The Radio shows the Guided tab, and the Yard shows its first job.

A narrower fix keeps the mode and the job, also small, in four files:
- When createdAt changes, imperativeStation.ts calls a refresh export of yardSim.js that runs buildPicker.
- Add profile.createdAt to the deps of the session effect at Drill.tsx:85.
- In RadioTest.tsx, restart the run on the same key.
verdict.ruledAlready: None. No known item or ruling covers a profile that is replaced while a station is open. RETRY-RESTART is a neighbour but covers a content reload, not a Reset or a Load. Two papers state the opposite intent. DECISIONS.md:360 says the picker is rebuilt "so the marks never go stale". D-0043 MASTERY-NOW says one value must be true at each place. The Y4b brief (specs/briefs/Y4b.md:44) accepts "shows at the next visit" for the sound choice only.

finding.title: The look-up dialog stays open over the next route after a browser Back, and closing it drops focus to the page body
finding.place: The look-up dialog (contract C1), opened from the Drill, the Yard refusal or the Radio test, then a browser history Back; 1440 and 390. src/components/LookUp.tsx does not watch the route. The C7 move of focus to the new heading fails while the modal is open.
finding.steps: Open the Drill, answer a question and press 'Look it up →'. While the dialog is open, go back in browser history (the browser Back button or Alt+Left). Then press Escape or Close, then Tab.
finding.happens: The route is Home ('Home — Clear Board'), but the dialog still shows the Drill's entry '435 SLOW TO STOP' over Home, and the session is gone. After Escape or Close, focus is on the page body, and the next Tab also leaves the page, so a keyboard user needs a third press to get back in. The Yard path gives the same result. The Settings dialog also stays open, but its focus returns to the Settings button.
finding.should: A change of route closes the look-up dialog, and focus goes to the heading of the new view, as C7 asks.
finding.evidence: p13.out: 'lookup-drill: after history back: route / dialog open true … after Escape: focus BODY … then Tab -> BODY'; the same lines for lookup-yard. Screenshot p21-back-dialog-390.png shows the dialog over Home at 390; 'after Close: focus BODY'.

verdict.evidence:
I reproduced it on the built app at dc88b14 (vite preview on 4566, Chromium, service workers blocked) at 1440x900 and 390x844. Steps: Home, then a station, then Enter on its "Look it up →", then history Back (page.goBack and history.back), then close by Escape, by a click on Close, or by Close + Enter. verdict.cause:
- src/components/LookUp.tsx:25-36. The dialog opens and closes only when lookUpRequest changes. Nothing closes it on a change of route, and the app context keeps the request across routes (src/state/AppContext.tsx:294-303). So after a history Back the modal stays over the new view.

verdict.cause: src/stations/yardSim.js:495. When still() is true, demoNextOfPlay calls demoStep() at once, so each next step runs inside the same click handler. Each step calls sayStep (:460-467), and sayStep writes the region at :465 through createLive().say (src/stations/yard/access.ts:95-101). say replaces textContent. All the writes land in one task with no frame between them, so the browser exposes only the last text to assistive tech.
verdict.fix:
About 10 lines, in src/stations/yardSim.js only:
- sayStep(k, before = '') writes `${before}${text} ${readout}.` to the region and returns it.
- demoStep(before = '') passes `before` to sayStep, then hands the returned message to demoNextOfPlay. For a move it hands it on only when the step ran still: `const said = sayStep(k, before), quiet = still(); animateMove(..., quiet, () => { paint(); demoNextOfPlay(quiet ? said : ''); })`.
- demoNextOfPlay(said = '') calls demoStep(said ? `${said} ` : '') when still() is true.

The last write of one "Play all" then holds each step it played, in order, as announce() does for the parts of one move (R7 F14). With motion on, nothing changes. The tested patch is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-clear-board/97369320-fcc4-5a82-bc9f-093035f8cbac/scratchpad/final-review/verify-access-13/fix.diff.

A larger alternative: hide "Play all" while Reduce motion is on (R7 7.18, "The stepper only"). That changes a control, and the control must follow the live setting.

1. /signals, 1440, seed 702. Screen 6 is the card "405 CLEAR SIGNAL · Proceed." with 3 drawings. Screen 7 is the question of sig.426. Screen 8 is the card "Rule 405 · Clear (405): Proceed. A single green — two greens is Clear to Medium (407), not Clear." Screen 9 is "What signal is this?" with a single green lamp on a mast. Its options are 408 CLEAR TO DIVERGING, 411 CLEAR TO STOP, 436 RESTRICTING and 405 CLEAR SIGNAL. Picking "405 CLEAR SIGNAL" gives "Right." The stored sig.405 is {seen 1, correct 1, interval 1}. It is the first signal item with correct > 0, so the cap test at store.ts:342 no longer applies. Signals mastery is 0.00068 either way, so no number on screen changes.

Picking "proceed at RESTRICTED speed" gives Right, and rule.436 is stored with correct 1. On /drill at 1440, seed 11507: the card "405 CLEAR SIGNAL · Proceed." comes right before "A single green (Clear, Rule 405) indicates…", and "Proceed" gives Right. (A first run showed "Not quite." here. That was my probe: Playwright's hasText matched "Proceed at restricted speed". With an exact match the app marks "Proceed" right.)

3. Correction: seeds 565 (1440) and 654 (390) give the screen order the finding states. But the drawings asked are a single yellow dwarf and a red over yellow dwarf. Of these, 215 are a rule card before a drawing question; 74 of the 215 describe the drawing asked (rule.405 and the single green mast 50, rule.436 and the staggered R-plate drawing 24), and 141 give only the name. The other 198 are a signal card before a rule question, and each holds the answer: "Proceed." for q.405.3 and "Proceed at RESTRICTED speed." for q.436.2. That is 2.04% of sessions, 1.35% with the answer on the card. On /drill: 0.17% and 0.10%. 6. Not new in kind. With the same question order and no cards, as before the wave, a twin question with its feedback stood right before a drawing question 198 times (76 describe the drawing). LEARN-GAP leaves it open, although its stated reason in D-0041 and the ruling ("a right answer right after the card is short-term memory, not a read on sight") is this exact case.

7. Severity is low, not medium. No content is wrong, no right answer is marked wrong, no progress is lost, and no control or flow breaks. The harm: in about 1 to 2% of first /signals sessions, an answer read off the screen before counts as a first read (interval 1, due in a day). And the SME is asked whether "one other screen" is enough without knowing that this screen can hold the answer.
